sections.overview: Crenicara punctulatum is a small South American cichlid widespread in the upper Amazon and also recorded in the Essequibo basin.
sections.identification: Its dark checkerboard flank pattern gives the species its common name; it is similar to C. latruncularium, which differs in several meristic and colour characters.
sections.habitat: It is recorded from forest creeks and sandy river shores, often near fallen leaves or among aquatic plants.
sections.diet: Kullander’s redescription does not provide a detailed natural prey inventory, so no specialized diet is assigned here.
sections.behavior: Claims that this species changes sex have appeared in older sources, but the status of C. punctulatum as a true sex-changing fish remains disputed.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs attached to plants or stones, and the female tends the clutch; reported egg numbers vary among compiled summaries.
sections.ecology: It is a benthopelagic freshwater fish of tropical lowland streams and shores, sharing its genus with the more localized C. latruncularium. A 2005 phylogeny places Crenicara with Dicrossus in the crenicarine clade; see Dicrossus maculatus.
sections.conservation: FishBase relays a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern; this status is distinct from the contested details of its reproductive biology.
